findings.namedBuyers: Amie Wright, Executive Director, is the strongest initial relationship contact: she is listed on the current team, signed the 2026 report and is explicitly invited to receive partnership inquiries at contact@torontocomics.com. Jalen Innis, Festival Producer, Logistics & Production, is a relevant operational referral for lodging logistics based on the published role (inference). Mandy Folsom, Festival Administrator, is an additional administrative routing contact. No source establishes that any named person controls hotel contracts.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced May 7–9, 2027 at Mattamy Athletic Centre. The About page distinguishes May 7 Libraries and Education Day / Word Balloon Academy from the May 8–9 public festival. These are activity dates within the requested horizon, not publication dates. The July 2026 wrap-up provisionally said June 2027; the later August announcement and current About page supersede that with May. No official 2028 edition was identified in the reviewed material.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment using the supplied hotel specifications: Radisson Blu’s 157 guestrooms and approximately 240-theatre largest room cannot house the festival exclusively or host its main marketplace. The organizer reports approximately 32,000 attendees in 2026; this is historical festival footfall, not a published unique overnight visitor count or room demand. A limited artist/publisher/staff cohort, speaker lodging or small side meeting is a plausible sales hypothesis, not verified demand. The Harbourfront hotel is not the venue-adjacent incumbent; Mattamy is at 50 Carlton Street and TCAF describes Courtyard as a 3–5 minute walk away. This is a city-festival lodging opportunity, not a resort programme. Do not assume catering or restaurant availability.
findings.venueCommitments: Announced main venue: Toronto Metropolitan University’s Mattamy Athletic Centre, 50 Carlton Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. This is downtown Toronto proper, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place, and is not a competing hotel. This establishes a published venue selection, not access to its signed contract. Ancillary 2027 venues and programme allocation have not been verified.
findings.historicalRotation: Toronto-based recurrence is verified, not merely inferred from an annual name. TCAF reports Toronto Reference Library hosting from 2009–2024; planned library renovations prompted the 2025 move to Mattamy Athletic Centre. The verified 2023–2027 sequence remains in Toronto: this is intra-city venue relocation, not evidence of destination rotation or a return-to-library commitment.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2027: unknown; no edition-specific hotel block, official housing bureau, open accommodation RFP or room quantity was identified. Historical organizer-arranged lodging is explicit. The 2025 booking page says: “We have arranged a room block for exhibitors, TCAF staff, and comics super friends at the Courtyard Marriott Toronto Downtown”; its cutoff was May 9, 2025 and it says “Booking Closed.” It warns the festival can incur attrition charges. The April 26, 2026 post says “we’ve arranged special pricing at the Marriott’s Courtyard Toronto Downtown,” the “location of our 2026 festival programming and special events”; that offer expired May 11, 2026. Every hotel named in these reviewed lodging sources: Courtyard Toronto Downtown, also styled Courtyard Marriott Toronto Downtown (one property). These are historical arrangements, not a 2027 booking commitment or proof that inventory is open.
findings.organizationStructure: TCAF describes itself as a “registered nonprofit, not a charity,” with its own Executive Director, festival production team and Board. It is the festival organizer, not the Mattamy venue or Courtyard hotel. The reviewed evidence does not identify an external PCO, DMC or housing agency. Do not equate nonprofit status with charitable registration or hotel-buying authority.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Courtyard Toronto Downtown has evidenced 2025 room-block and 2026 lodging/programming incumbency, plus the organizer-published short walk to Mattamy. Its integrated programme role is a competitive advantage (assessment), but no 2027 renewal, exclusivity, sold-out condition, capacity shortfall or overflow requirement is established. No published peak rooms, room nights or contracted block size was found. Do not convert 32,000 festival attendees into hotel demand.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Amie Wright through the published contact@torontocomics.com partnership route and request an introduction to Jalen Innis and the person responsible for 2027 hotel sourcing. Ask whether Courtyard is renewed, whether any supplementary cohort is unplaced, actual peak rooms/room nights, stay pattern, budget, payment/attrition terms, and whether a Harbourfront location is acceptable. Only then scope a modest block against hotel availability; 15–109 peak rooms is a supplied product-fit range, not an event forecast. Offer side-meeting options only after operational and catering checks. If 2027 is committed, obtain the next lodging review date rather than treating it as an open lead.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the target 2027 edition, dates and main venue are confirmed publicly, but a sales-accessible hotel requirement is not. The venue-selection path is not an open main-event bid. Supplementary lodging or ancillary meetings can only be explored through organizer qualification; historical Courtyard bookings do not prove that 2027 is either locked or open.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: recurring Toronto editions and demonstrated organizer-arranged lodging justify developing a future-cycle relationship. Position Radisson Blu as a supplementary artist/publisher or executive group option rather than attempting to replace Mattamy or claiming all-festival housing. Any future incumbent displacement depends on the organizer’s renewal timetable, price, transport needs and actual room production; no 2028 dates or hotel opportunity are verified.
